samples.summary: Concurrent CLI logins clobber the single `wafflebase_cli_confirm` cookie, so the older consent page's Continue click silently re-asks
samples.evidence: The delta hardens the consent page (frame/cache headers) and pins its Continue link, making the page's click the load-bearing step. But the confirm half is stored under one fixed cookie name (`CLI_CONFIRM_COOKIE`, guard:37) issued per render (guard:284). Two overlapping `wafflebase login` runs — the exact scenario the neighbouring comment at guard:19-31 says motivated giving the CLI *state* cookie its own name — overwrite each other: clicking Continue on the first page presents a token that no longer matches the cookie, `hasConfirmation` (guard:313-325) returns false, and the guard silently renders a *third* consent page (issuing yet another cookie, invalidating page two). The user sees the consent screen again with no explanation, and each retry invalidates the other tab, so a user alternating tabs never completes a login. The same happens on a double-click of Continue, since the confirmed start clears the cookie (guard:290) before redirecting.

samples.summary: Corrected comment still names the bare cookie, not the `__Host-` wire name actually used on https deployments
samples.evidence: The delta fixes the comment to `wafflebase_cli_state`, but `loginCookieName` (github-auth.guard.ts:92-97) prefixes `__Host-` whenever `secureCookies()` is true, so the wire name on any https deployment is `__Host-wafflebase_cli_state`. A reader debugging a rejected callback by grepping for the documented name will not find it.
